This art's border ring is 100% frame/stone material (a continuous shaded surface, L 15-59, no separable flat background at any tolerance tried: 12/6/3 all ate progressively more of the frame down to unrecognizable fragments). Exit is a structural doorway meant to fill the cell, so it's shipped as the raw generated tile with every pixel's alpha clamped to 255 (the raw source already had 0 non-opaque pixels, so this was a no-op clamp, not a visible change).

That tile was fully discarded in favour of the round-3 reroll above, not patched.

postProcessingTools.seam: band_score (per-axis std of column/row mean luma) + edge/interior gradient ratio; --repair does a two-stage fix (flatten low-frequency per-column/row luma drift, then an eased cross-dissolve only if the edge-crossing gradient is still abnormal)
postProcessingTools.match: palette_match -- remaps to the reference's hue families (Lab-nearest), matches mean luma, preserves each pixel's own deviation from its source's mean (keeps contrast instead of crushing it flat)
postProcessingTools.grade: compute_grade / apply_grade -- ONE uniform Lab (L-offset, chroma-scale) transform from a single sample-vs-reference comparison, applied identically across a whole tile family
postProcessingTools.cutout: border-ring Lab-colour clustering + border-connected flood fill (only background reachable from the edge is removed) + optional keep_dark_l (never cut a pixel darker than L, regardless of border-connectivity -- protects an intentional near-black void subject that touches the tile edge) + sides (restrict which edges count as 'known background', for a subject designed to reach some edges on purpose)
postProcessingTools.cleanalpha: binarize alpha at threshold 128 (no partial/fringe pixels), remove stray opaque connected-components smaller than min_speck px (protecting the single largest component as the main subject), fill enclosed transparent pinholes smaller than min_hole px (coloured from the mean of their opaque rim). Runs by default at the end of cutout() (clean=True); feather is off by default (DEFAULT_CUTOUT_FEATHER=0) since a soft alpha ramp reads as anti-aliased blur, not a clean pixel-art cut.
postProcessingTools.pack: scripts/tiles/pack.py <spec.json> <out_dir> -- packs a biome's terrain tiles into terrain.png (8-wide sheet) + terrain.json (TerrainManifest); spec.desaturate blends every packed tile toward its own luminance by that amount, alpha untouched
